name: Nevada
summary: A cobalt blue field with a silver star in the upper hoist, the word 'NEVADA' beneath it, inside two sagebrush branches, with a gold scroll reading 'Battle Born' above.
origin: Louis Shellback III won a 1926 design contest; the flag was adopted in 1929. In 1991 the law was amended to place the letters of 'NEVADA' below the star instead of between its points.

colors.name: Silver
colors.meaning: The star; Nevada is the Silver State.

symbols.name: Silver star
symbols.description: A five-pointed star in the canton.

symbols.name: Sagebrush
symbols.description: Two branches of the state flower.

symbols.name: 'Battle Born' scroll
symbols.description: A gold ribbon above the star.
symbols.meaning: Nevada became a state in 1864, during the Civil War.

facts: Nevada's statehood was rushed through in 1864 partly to help re-elect Abraham Lincoln.
The Silver State's name means 'snow-covered' in Spanish.
Before 1991, the letters of NEVADA were placed between the star's points.
clues: Cobalt blue with a silver star in sagebrush and a gold 'Battle Born' scroll.
Its scroll says it became a state during a civil war.
Its star honours a precious metal.
